artboards.title: Day view — h/l steps the day

annotations.text: Today, with LOG added below DANGLING. Order is decisions first, record last — the log carries no status because there is nothing in it to decide.

The day view. h/l and ←/→ already reach onMoveRequested and are thrown away today (`if (dy !== 0)`), so the day axis costs one binding.

TODAY/DANGLING collapse into one TODO list here: "dangling" is a relationship to today, which a past day doesn't have.

c is free — it was "done" until that moved to x.

The dot is the point of the grid: a past day still carrying open todos is drawn in urgent, so a month reads as a debt map rather than a date picker. Dim numbers are days with no note at all.

Enter opens the day; the panel already routes Enter to activateRequested, so calendar mode just claims it the way settings claims letters.

Two CLI gaps before any of this ships:

1. Notes are write-only — tasks_in only ever reads cfg["section"], so nothing reads `## Log` back. Both LOG sections need a read path.

2. The grid needs per-day counts in ONE pass — 30 `list --day` processes a month is not it. scan(cfg, since, until) already walks a range in one go, so a `bujo days 2026-09 --json` returning {day, open, done, notes} is a thin wrapper over what exists.

Not chosen, kept for the record.

Day rail — a picker first, a day second. Costs a second cursor model inside 360px: j/k means "pick a day" up top and "pick a row" below. The calendar does this job better, and only when asked for.

Timeline — no mode at all, which was the appeal. But the panel stops being a decision surface and becomes a feed, and `a` (add) loses an obvious day to land on.
